item.title: Trump BLAMES Biden as Aviation Crisis Grounds America (ft. Maggie Haberman)
item.description:
Jessica Tarlov is joined by New York Times reporter Maggie Haberman to break down the growing turmoil inside Trump’s administration, the fight over Democratic leadership, and why Trump may be losing support from the podcast crowd that helped elect him.
After thousands of flights were canceled and grounded nationwide and more than a million passengers were disrupted, the shutdown exposed just how urgently the country needs to modernize its decades-old air traffic control system.
But as the crisis unfolded, Trump was largely silent. While Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin faced reporters, the administration blamed Biden and demanded billions more in funding. Is Trump focused more on his legacy than the current state of affairs?
After a colossal midterms defeat, Trump is shaking up his cabinet. The president fired his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, earlier this month, replacing her with immigration hardliner Stephen Miller. Are more shakeups on the horizon?
With Trump’s upcoming trip to China, there are some new questions about who will be in the president’s inner circle. How will the drama at Nvidia impact the meeting between Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin?
There may be a serious challenge brewing to Chuck Schumer’s leadership: Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen. Is Van Hollen a credible alternative to Schumer for Democrats?

item.title: Trump’s China Strategy BACKFIRES as Jensen Huang Eyes Nvidia Return
item.description:
Scott Galloway and Jessica Tarlov break down the latest political news: Trump’s trip to Asia, more fallout from the FAA ground stop, and a series of other digital infrastructure problems.
Trump arrived in the Philippines ahead of a crucial trilateral meeting in China. His meetings with world leaders come as tensions brew over advanced AI chips illicitly sold by Nvidia. How will concern for America’s technological advantage complicate negotiations with Xi Jinping? And how much leverage does China have over the United States in the AI race?
Meanwhile, it’s been a rough week for America’s aging technology infrastructure. After a nearly-unprecedented hourslong FAA ground stop last week, many banks and individual airlines experienced new problems with their online services. Plus, a major setback for public health in America: the U.S. has officially lost its measles-elimination status for the first time in 26 years. Is RFK Jr. to blame?
With the pending release of his new book Promise Me, America, former President Biden defends his decision to stay in the 2024 race as long as he did. Amazon MGM has greenlit yet another media property centered on (and executive produced by) First Lady Melania Trump. And, in a shift in a certain niche of independent media, Trump seems to be losing the support of a key part of his 2024 coalition: podcast bros. What caused such a shift, and is this a bright spot for Dems?

item.title: Trump’s AUTOCRAT PLAYDATE with Xi and Putin DELIVERS NOTHING
item.description:
Scott Galloway and Jessica Tarlov discuss Trump’s summit with Xi and Putin, Anthropic’s IPO, the ongoing Nvidia scandal, and what Democrats are positioning for with their majorities in the next Congress.
Trump has departed China after a historic first-of-its-kind summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. But despite the extraordinary concentration of geopolitical power in the room, the talks produced no major diplomatic breakthroughs. With the New START treaty having expired in February 2026, the three countries face a new and potentially dangerous chapter in nuclear competition. Scott and Jessica examine the optics of Trump's unusually warm relationship with Putin, the diplomatic advantages Russia and China may have gained, and the absence of Ukraine and European allies from the negotiating table. Did Trump secure anything meaningful for the United States, or did Putin and Xi walk away with the bigger victory?
Next, Scott looks into updates on the Jensen Huang scandal, including a petition to reinstate the Nvidia executive garnering over 100,000 signatures. What does this mean for the state of gender parity within the corporate culture of big tech? Scott argues that calls for Huang's return overlook the importance of workplace accountability, board oversight, and national security. With NVIDIA's underlying AI business still attracting enormous demand, is the company better off moving forward without its founder at the helm?
Meanwhile, back on Wall Street, Anthropic, the company behind Claude, has made history with an IPO priced at $83 per share, valuing the AI company at approximately $1.5 trillion and raising a record-breaking $81 billion. The company's prospectus devotes extensive attention to risk disclosures, and its public listing brings additional reporting obligations and shareholder scrutiny. Could going public actually make one of the world's most powerful AI companies safer and more transparent, or will the pressure to deliver returns ultimately outweigh its safety commitments? How could this impact AI policy debate in Washington?
Democrats are preparing to take control of Congress following a sweeping midterm victory, with their Senate majority now standing at 56–44 after Mary Peltola's victory in Alaska. House Democrats have formally nominated Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker, putting him on track to become the first Black Speaker of the House in American history. Meanwhile, incoming House Oversight Chairman Robert Garcia is preparing an aggressive investigative agenda, sending document-preservation letters to 12 people in Trump’s orbit. But will Trump pardon his family before they face consequences?
After spending hundreds of millions of dollars supporting Republican candidates and previously embracing the MAGA movement, Elon Musk is suddenly distancing himself from the Trump political brand. Saying that both parties have positives and negatives, and that Washington would benefit from a divided government. Is Musk really changing his tune, or just trying to protect himself from potential investigations?
Finally, Jess and Scott take your questions on Marco Rubio, the debut of GTA 6, and dating apps.
